ground.name: Triều Phượng Đỉnh
ground.gloss: Summit Where the Birds Pay Homage to the Phoenix

ground.name: Đan Sơn Mạch
ground.note: Sơn Hải Kinh's cinnabar mountain is where the phoenix is born. 3 tiles from Thiên Xu's border.

ground.name: Cao Cương Phong
ground.note: Kinh Thi: phượng hoàng minh hĩ, vu bỉ cao cương, the phoenix sings on that high ridge. A sacred summit (Light).

ground.name: Chu Sa Tuyền
ground.note: A red hot spring in the jungle of Đan Huyệt Châu, the phoenix's cinnabar land.

ground.name: Vân Môn Thành
ground.note: Cửu Thiều's city, named for the ancient Vân Môn music, twin of the Thiều; abandoned after the War of the Nine Shao.

ground.name: Đan Thạch Khoáng
ground.note: Red stone from the phoenix's cinnabar land, Đan Huyệt Châu.

ground.name: Tương Phi Đảo
ground.note: Its spotted bamboo, stained by the tears of the two consorts of Thuấn

ground.name: Thiều Âm Thị
ground.note: The music that brings the phoenix; below Phượng Minh Cung's seat

ground.name: Triêu Hà Hồ
ground.note: The east's dawn clouds answer Lạc Hà's sunset clouds in the west; beside Lễ Tuyền Phái

ground.name: Vạn Xà Lâm
ground.note: Deep jungle at the far end of Đan Huyệt Châu, the farthest lair from any town.

ground.name: Chúc Dung Khẩu
ground.note: Named for the fire god; a vent on the east coast of Đan Huyệt Châu.

events.text_en: Mạc Quy Khư, a Kết Đan cultivator of 240, enters the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh on Dục Nhật Đảo at its first recorded opening; the Thiên Nguyên calendar counts its years from that day.
The first fishers of the gulf see the sun rise out of the sea at Dục Nhật Đảo, and believe it bathes there every night.
Cửu Thiều builds Vân Môn Thành on the plain, named for the Vân Môn music, the Thiều's twin; the stone chime Vân Môn Khánh hangs in its hall.
Rice is first planted in the flooded fields of the plain; Thủy Điền's paddies are older than every sect but two.
Vân Môn's musicians play to the morning sun over the lake, and the dawn clouds take the colour of the music.
Mulberry fields planted in the red soil at Tang Điền feed the silkworms of the south.
Tôn Hà Khởi founds Xích Thành Môn among the red cliffs and vents of Đan Huyệt Châu, where the rock rises like a rosy cloud.
Xích Thành Môn weaves its war banner, the Xích Hà Kỳ, from fire-silk spun in the vents.
Red stone from Đan Thạch is cut for Xích Thành's walls.
Xích Thành Môn builds Ngũ Thải Thành on the coast of Đan Huyệt Châu.
The students of Trúc Địch Viện, Cửu Thiều Cung's flute school, go up to the palace's last stand and do not come back.
In the War of the Nine Shao, Cửu Thiều Cung's drum fort Minh Cổ Bảo falls; Phượng Minh leaves it as it fell.
The hall of Cửu Thiều Cung's chime makers, Kích Khánh Đường, is smashed in the war; its broken chimes still ring when stepped on.
Vân Môn Thành empties within a year; its people take the music with them and scatter to the four coasts.
A year after Cửu Thiều Cung falls, the flute sellers of Tiêu Sơn Thị have all gone, and the market is never resettled.
With Cửu Thiều Cung fallen, the jade-pipe makers of Ngọc Quản Trấn leave, and the oak woods take the town.
The great Bằng is said to rest on Đồ Nam Đảo before its flight to the south.
Wild peach trees grow over the empty palace grounds; the brook below is named Đào Khê.
Yellow oxen run wild on the empty plain; the village that tames them is called Hoàng Ngưu.
Gulls and herons crowd the shore at Âu Lộ; fishers say the birds were there before the sects and will be after.
Ngô Thê Đồng founds Phượng Minh Cung on the lands left empty since the fall of Cửu Thiều Cung, 140 years before.
Phượng Minh's founder clears the ridges and opens a market of the Shao music at the foot of the new palace: Thiều Âm Thị.
Ngô Thê Đồng finds the Tiêu Thiều Quản in the ruins of Cửu Thiều's palace, and tells no one.
The spotted bamboo on Tương Phi Đảo is said to be stained by the tears of two consorts; Phượng Minh forbids cutting it.

In Thạch Kiều Thành, Chung Hoài Cực sets the North Star Compact before the seven sects and stamps it with the Bắc Thần Ấn: land changes hands only by a fall, a gift, an oath or a war the Pivot licenses by writ, and Thiên Xu Tông will enforce it.
The Vương family, rivals of the Tạ in another land, settle among the rice of Đạo Hương and plant a field each generation.
Phượng Minh Cung takes the rice plain of Triêu Dương Nguyên, empty since Cửu Thiều fell.
Wheat fields at Mạch Điền feed the new palace; the town grows around its granary.
Phượng Minh Cung founds Lai Nghi Thành on the plain, where the phoenix comes when the music is played nine times.
Plum blossom at Lý Hoa Thôn is so white that snow geese land among it by mistake.
Phượng Minh Cung founds Thanh Khê Thành, its port on the gulf.
Tôn Hà Khởi dies; his heir Chu Liệt Nhật turns Xích Thành Môn to burning villages to feed its fire arts.
Phượng Minh Cung asks the Pivot for a writ against Xích Thành Môn, which has burned eleven villages; the first writ of the Compact is granted.
In the War of the Vermilion Caves, the villagers of Cúc Viên hide Phượng Minh's scouts among the chrysanthemums.
In the War of the Vermilion Caves, Xích Thành Môn's men fire their quarry town of Tạc Thạch Trấn rather than leave it; the quarrymen who stay build Thạch Tượng below.
Phượng Minh destroys Xích Thành Môn with Chu Liệt Nhật; Đan Huyệt Châu and Ngũ Thải Thành pass to Phượng Minh, and the Xích Hà Kỳ hangs in its hall.
Hỏa Ti Trấn, where the fire-silk was reeled from the vents, burns in the fighting as Phượng Minh destroys Xích Thành Môn; no one spins fire-silk there again.
With Xích Thành Môn fallen, its sea hall Viêm Hải Quán is abandoned, and Phượng Minh never reopens it.
Lưu Hỏa Các, Xích Thành Môn's fire hall on the volcanic isle, is abandoned when the gate falls.
Phượng Minh's disciples climb Cao Cương Phong at dawn and say the phoenix sang there, on that high ridge.
The mulberry shade at Tang Âm becomes the resting place of the silk caravans.
Phượng Minh Cung founds Hoàng Vân Thành, the granary of the rice plain.
Phượng Minh Cung builds the pearl harbour Châu Lệ Cảng on its eastern coast.
Ô Kình Hải gathers pirates on an islet of the southern gulf and founds Thôn Hải Môn, the Gate That Swallows the Sea.
Hoàng Vân Thành's granaries feed the south through a seven-year drought; Phượng Minh's rice becomes its strength.
Healers who brew wine from the sweet spring the phoenix drinks found Lễ Tuyền Phái.
The green meadows of Lục Dã are given to Lễ Tuyền Phái for its herb gardens.
The river bend at Hà Loan floods every autumn; its people build their houses on stilts.
A ginkgo at Ngân Hạnh Thôn turns gold in a single night every autumn; it is older than the village.
Mạc Quy Khư comes to live on Dục Nhật Đảo by the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh, and never leaves it again.
Băng Tâm Các and Phượng Minh Cung go to war over the caravan road between the desert and the rice plain.
Cô Thành's garrison holds out for two years against Phượng Minh's fire, drinking the desert lake down to salt.
Phượng Minh's fire breaks Cô Thành; the lone fortress falls and the desert lake turns to salt.
In the year Cô Thành falls, Phượng Minh's fire breaks Băng Tâm's beacon fort of Lang Yên Bảo on the caravan road.
The Pivot imposes a truce on the Desert Road; the caravans pass again, and the border stays where it was.
Spirit farmers found Trúc Thực Viên to grow the bamboo seed the phoenix eats.
Thôn Hải's pirates burn Châu Lệ Cảng; the pearl harbour's divers flee, and the pearls in the moonlit sea are said to weep.
The pearl divers of burned Châu Lệ Cảng settle inland at Âu Lộ and never dive again.
Thôn Hải's pirates burn the salt town of Hải Diêm Trấn, two years after Châu Lệ Cảng; its salt makers never come back.
Thôn Hải's raiders carry off the whole village of Lô Châu; only the reed cutters hidden in the marsh escape.
Thôn Hải's raiders burn the mangrove town of Bàn Căn Trấn, and the mangroves take it back.
Thôn Hải's pirates burn the spice port of Hương Phàm Trấn; the Purge comes ten years too late for it, and its trade moves to Hương Liệu.
Đỗ Tinh Hà calls the Pirate Purge; Phượng Minh's and Lạc Hà's fleets sail under the Pivot's writ, and Thạch Cơ Thành rises around their stone jetty.
Phượng Minh's fleet burns Ẩn Phàm Trại, the shore camp where Thôn Hải Môn hid its boats, a year before the Purge.
The Purge ends at Thôn Hải Môn: Ô Kình Hải dies on his islet and his sabre Kình Nha is lost in the burning hold.
Captives freed from Thôn Hải's hold return to Lô Châu and rebuild it reed by reed.
After the Purge, Phượng Minh withdraws the garrison of Liệu Phàm Bảo, and the empty fort begins to crumble into the gulf.
Survivors of the pirate years found Vọng Triều Đường by the burned piers of Châu Lệ, swearing no harbour on this coast will burn again.
Jade-green waves at Bích Lãng carry the fishing boats home from the gulf.
A fever kills half of Cựu Khê Trấn before Lễ Tuyền's healers come; the survivors move down to Thanh Khê and never go back up.
Lava from the vent above runs over the lower courts of the empty Lưu Hỏa Các, and only its roofs still show.
Mai Lễ Tuyền is born in Lục Dã Trấn; they say her first cry made the spring flow sweeter.
Phượng Minh finds the Cinnabar Mountain vein near its border with the heart and names it Đan Sơn Mạch.
The lake at Hồ Tâm rises and falls with the tide, though it touches no sea; Phượng Minh's scholars cannot say why.
A great storm tide drowns Kim Sa Trấn on the golden beach; its people move inland, and their grandchildren become the dyers of Lam Điện.
Hoa Triêu Dương is born at dawn on the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ as the clouds turn red.
Hùng Phần Vũ is born in Ngũ Thải Thành; a red feather falls on his cradle.
The young Hùng Phần Vũ founds Phần Vũ Đường in the vents where Xích Thành once stood; Phượng Minh lends it the Xích Hà Kỳ.
Phần Vũ Đường's disciples sit in the vents until their feathers burn and walk out reborn; the first of them dies trying.
Phượng Minh Cung goes to war with Thính Vũ Lâu for the Kinh Lôi vein.
In the Thunder Vein War Phượng Minh's disciples take and burn Thủ Lôi Bảo; when the vein is kept, the Tower builds its new guard higher on the ridge.
In the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's raiders reach the upper ferry at Thượng Độ before the Pivot's envoys stop them.
The Pivot ends the Thunder Vein War: Thính Vũ keeps the vein, and the south remembers.
Ninh Trúc Thực becomes head of Trúc Thực Viên and breeds a bamboo that seeds every year instead of once in sixty.
Hoàng Vân Thành's granaries are opened to Băng Tâm's desert in a famine year, and the old Desert Road quarrel is quietly forgotten.
In the great rains the hillside slides and buries the millstone town of Thạch Ma Trấn in a night; the survivors go down to Lục Dã.
Pilgrims come by boat to Dục Nhật Đảo to ask the hermit Mạc Quy Khư about the world before the sects; he answers one question a year.
Ngô Thê Đồng dies at 770; Hoa Triêu Dương becomes head of Phượng Minh Cung.
Dying, Ngô Thê Đồng gives Hoa Triêu Dương the Tiêu Thiều Quản and tells her never to play it in full.
Bird catchers who say all birds bow to the phoenix found Bách Vũ Các to raise messenger birds for Phượng Minh's palace.
Lễ Tuyền Phái's spirit wine is served at the Pivot's table for the first time; Thiên Xu orders a hundred jars a year.
Thính Vũ Lâu attacks Đan Sơn Mạch, Phượng Minh's cinnabar vein near the heart.
Weavers sworn to Phượng Minh found Chức Hà Các and weave fire-silk from Tang Điền's worms without the vents; the palace has not yet decided if that pleases it.
Doãn Ngọc Hành brings Thiên Xu Tông into the war on Phượng Minh's side, to enforce the Compact.
In the Cinnabar Vein War, Thanh Khê Thành's harbour shelters Phượng Minh's wounded; the city's lanterns burn all year.
Thính Vũ Lâu is beaten at Đan Sơn Mạch and withdraws; Mạnh Dạ Vũ swears the Pivot will answer for it.
Quan Vũ Thanh, first elder of Thính Vũ, travels to Phượng Minh in secret to talk of peace, and comes back without an answer.
Thạch Cơ Thành's stone jetty cracks in a storm; Phượng Minh rebuilds it with stone from the ruins of Xích Thành.
A musician in Thiều Âm Thị plays a tune no one taught him, and every bird on the ridge falls silent; Phượng Minh's elders pay his passage far away.
The Vương clan of Đạo Hương sends a letter of betrothal to the Tạ of Phong Lâm; the reply has not yet come.

wars.name: War of the Vermilion Caves
wars.outcome: Xích Thành Môn had turned to burning villages; Phượng Minh fights it under Thiên Xu's writ and takes Đan Huyệt Châu.

wars.name: Desert Road War
wars.outcome: Over the caravan road between Cô Yên Mạc and Triêu Dương Nguyên. Thiên Xu imposes a truce; no land changes.

wars.name: The Pirate Purge
wars.outcome: Called and led by Thiên Xu with Phượng Minh's and Lạc Hà's fleets; the ma đạo pirates of Thôn Hải Môn are destroyed.

wars.name: Thunder Vein War
wars.outcome: Phượng Minh tries to take Kinh Lôi Mạch; the Pivot ends the war and Thính Vũ keeps the vein.

wars.name: Cinnabar Vein War
wars.outcome: Thính Vũ attacks Phượng Minh's Đan Sơn Mạch; Thiên Xu steps in on Phượng Minh's side and Thính Vũ is beaten.

cast.name: Hoa Triêu Dương
cast.gloss: The phoenix sings to the morning sun (Thi Kinh)

build.note: The brave, ambitious Phoenix head: a phoenix that burns and is reborn, the panpipes she must never play in full

cast.name: Ngô Thê Đồng
cast.gloss: The phoenix perches on the parasol tree
cast.role: Founder of Phượng Minh Cung (year 480, at 150)

cast.name: Vu Ngô Đồng
cast.gloss: The parasol tree where the phoenix perches
cast.role: First elder of Phượng Minh Cung (age 320)

build.note: The wutong where the phoenixes roost: a generous, impatient beast tamer whose spirit birds fight for him

legendary_items.story: Cửu Thiều's mind-bending instrument, the cause of the Nine Shao judgement. Phượng Minh found it on the empty land; Thiên Xu does not know.
legendary_items.name: Tiêu Thiều Quản
legendary_items.secret: Thiên Xu destroyed a sect over it
